cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and what you understand is turning into what you show.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Turn something you cleared or worked out lately into a first rough version — a page, a plan, one finished attempt. Rough is fine. Put it where it could be seen, even if nobody looks.
cells.core:
Where the pull toward something better meets what you've already worked out, the understanding has somewhere to go. You can mark the shallow water for other people — say where the crossing runs and which way is through. That's the shape of this: careful thinking that has stopped being only yours and has started being useful.

What it wants now is a first built thing, not a better map. Take one piece you've already cleared and make the roughest real version of it — a page, a plan, a draft that could be read. It doesn't need to be finished or shown. Building it is what keeps the pull from turning into more thinking about the pull.
cells.sheetLine: What you've worked out wants a shape you can point at.
cells.verb: Charting passage for others from what you already know.
cells.place: Where the pull toward light orients you before you've earned it.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a crossing that has not asked to be made yet.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Find the part you keep circling without touching. Give it one honest sitting, on purpose. Then put in a line what actually held, and drop the rest of the approach without dropping the aim.
cells.core:
The pull to rise is running out past the ground it stands on. You're charting the whole route before any water has been checked — preparing for a passage that isn't here, and from inside that reads as discipline. It keeps you busy, and it keeps you from finding out what's actually solid.

So test it on purpose. Take the one piece you keep going around and go straight at it for one sitting. Not to win it — to see what holds when you lean your weight. Put in a line what held, and let go of whatever method didn't. What survives the friction is the commitment. What doesn't was only the way you were doing it.
cells.sheetLine: The crossing you're steering is still ahead of you.
cells.verb: Charting passage for others from what you already know.
cells.place: Where the pull toward light orients you before you've earned it.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that shut behind you, and the pen is down.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: Stop waiting for a feeling to show you the way. Take the plain call within reach and make it — nobody consulted first — then let it stand without relitigating it.
cells.core:
The pull toward something better has gone quiet, and nothing is being decided. You're waiting at a closed door for a feeling that used to arrive and show you the way. While you wait, the small calls stack up unmade, and the waiting itself starts to look like the whole stance.

Nothing here flows while it stays unanswered. There's a plain call within reach that doesn't need a feeling under it — make it, no one consulted first. It doesn't have to be large, and it doesn't have to be inspired. The right thing doesn't argue its case; it just gets done, and then you're on the other side of it, which is further than waiting ever gets you.
cells.sheetLine: Make the plain call. The feeling can come later.
cells.verb: Charting passage for others from what you already know.
cells.place: Where the pull toward light orients you before you've earned it.

cells.tense: You are pointing the way for people and letting that read as your personality rather than your work.
cells.act: let the vision be shared with one other
cells.ask: Say your own heading out loud to someone who'll keep it — the direction you're actually steering by, not the advice you'd hand them. Once, plainly, like a fact you're stating.
cells.core:
You're charting passage for others all the time — steadying them, showing where the crossing runs — and it happens so continuously that it stops looking like work. Seen well, this is careful thinking put in service, and it's useful to whoever is standing next to you. What's happening now is that the directing runs on without your hand visibly on it; the usefulness keeps arriving and you keep talking about it as though it were simply how you're built.

The smaller move is to name your own heading. What you see for the road you're on, said to one person who'll keep it, once, plainly. The pull toward light gets strongest just before it's given words, and when it stays unspoken it drains you quietly. Saying it once is the part that's yours.
cells.sheetLine: Name the heading you're actually steering by, once.
cells.verb: Charting passage for others from what you already know.
cells.place: Where the pull toward light orients you before you've earned it.
